source.title: The Art of Public Speaking
source.author: Dale Carnegie and J. Berg Esenwein
source.summary: A practical public-speaking manual about confidence, preparation, delivery, persuasion, voice, audience attention, and clear argument.
source.corePromise: Help readers turn clear thinking into spoken influence.

target.positioning: communication, demos, pitches, meetings, webinars, technical talks, and leadership presence for builders and operators

us.evidence: Published in 1915, well before the 1930 U.S. public-domain cutoff active in 2026.

subtitleOptions: A Modern Guide to Demos, Pitches, Meetings, and Clear Technical Communication
Public Speaking Rebuilt for Founders, Developers, Operators, and Creators
How to Turn Clear Thinking Into Spoken Influence
adaptation.modernWorld: Remote meetings, product demos, technical talks, sales calls, investor pitches, webinars, podcasts, async video, and team leadership
toneRules: Make communication practical, direct, and useful for people who build.
Translate stage-era advice into demos, meetings, launches, and technical explanations.
Keep the voice confident without sounding theatrical or manipulative.
prohibitedChanges: Do not imply the original authors wrote this adaptation.
Do not teach manipulation or deceptive persuasion.
Do not preserve dated gender, platform, or stage assumptions when modernizing examples.
coreLessons: Clear speech begins with clear thinking.
Confidence is built through preparation and repeated exposure.
Audience attention must be earned quickly and held with structure.
Concrete examples persuade better than abstractions.
Voice, pacing, and presence affect trust.
A strong talk moves listeners toward a specific action.
The speaker's character and sincerity shape the message.

chapterPlan.title: The Fear of the Room
chapterPlan.focus: Reframe stage fright as a manageable system problem.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: A founder freezes during a product demo and learns how preparation reduces fear.

chapterPlan.title: Think Before You Talk
chapterPlan.focus: Show that clear speaking comes from clear structure.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Technical ideas become memorable when organized around one promise, one audience, and one next action.

chapterPlan.title: Make the Abstract Concrete
chapterPlan.focus: Teach examples, stories, demos, and analogies.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Developers explain complex systems to customers, investors, and nontechnical teams.

chapterPlan.title: Hold the Room
chapterPlan.focus: Translate attention, gesture, voice, and pacing into modern presentation habits.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Zoom calls, webinars, podcast appearances, conference talks, and live sales calls.

chapterPlan.title: Persuasion Without Theater
chapterPlan.focus: Show how sincerity, evidence, and usefulness create influence.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: A builder pitches adoption without hype.

chapterPlan.title: The Talk That Ships
chapterPlan.modernFrame: A good presentation creates decisions, buy-in, sales, funding, recruiting, or better execution.
